  echo: false

---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(here)
ili <- read.csv(here("raw_data", "example_ili.csv"))
ili$week <- as.Date(ili$week)
peak <- ili[which.max(ili$pct_ili), ]
```

::: {.callout-note}
All data in this report is made up, for practice only.
:::

## Summary

Across `{r} length(unique(ili$county))` counties and `{r} length(unique(ili$week))` weeks, the highest weekly ILI was **`{r} peak$pct_ili`%** in `{r} peak$county` County, the week of `{r} format(peak$week, "%B %d, %Y")`.

## Trend

```{r}
#| label: fig-trend
#| fig-cap: "Weekly percent of visits for ILI, Clark County"
#| fig-alt: "Line chart of weekly percent of visits for influenza-like illness in Clark County over 20 weeks, rising from under 2% in early October to a peak around 4% to 5% in December, then falling."
clark <- subset(ili, county == "Clark")
plot(clark$week, clark$pct_ili, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Week", ylab = "% of visits for ILI")
```
